newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ dollar closes a touch firmer in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: NZ dollar closes a touch firmer in thin trade.

text.p: The New Zealand dollar closed slightly stronger on Monday in very quiet trading affected by holidays in Auckland and Australia.
The Kiwi closed at US$0.6931/38, up from 0.6928/35 at the open, after trading a 0.6925-46 range during the day. It closed at 67.87 on its Trade-Weighted Index, up from 67.83.

Dealers said current account data released on Monday, which showed the current account in deficit by NZ$2.17 billion in the September quarter and $4.2 billion for the September year, could create some uncertainty offshore.
Economists had forecast a quarterly deficit of $1.71 billion and an annual deficit of $3.71 billion.

"I don't think the locals were terrribly fazed by it but with the number getting up to 4.6 percent of GDP, it is the sort of thing that might start to attract a little attention offshore," said one dealer.
"Given the Kiwi has broken below some fairly important longer term technical levels it may conspire to create a little weakness over the short to medium term," he said.
Dealers expected the Kiwi to trade $0.6915-50 range overnight. "I can't see a lot happening until we come back tomorrow to be honest," the dealer said.
